Story: Berkeley River Lodge caretakers take on job again despite cyclone
What happened: Caretakers Laura Stokes and Adam Zerna sheltered 18 hours in an underground container as Cyclone Fina wrecked Berkeley River Lodge in 2025.
How it ended: The couple stayed to help rebuild; the lodge reopened in May after 150 days, and they are back as caretakers.

Story: Ukraine: Dramatic night rescue pulls woman from rubble after 22 hours
What happened: Valentyna, 79, was trapped for 22 hours under concrete slabs in a five-storey apartment building in Dymer hit by a Russian drone strike.
How it ended: Rescuers with sniffer dogs pulled her out alive overnight and handed her to paramedics, who took her to hospital.

Story: No qualifying stories
'We live in fear' — Russian attack near Kyiv kills 10, leaves families waiting as rescuers search rubble
What happened: A Russian drone strike collapsed an apartment building in Dymer, trapping seven-year-old David under the rubble for nearly 14 hours.
How it ended: Rescuers pulled David out alive; the interior minister said he is in stable condition and receiving medical care.

Story: New documentary: Princess Kate speaks candidly about how cancer changed her body and mind
What happened: Catherine, Princess of Wales, was diagnosed with cancer in March 2024 after major abdominal surgery and had preventative chemotherapy.
How it ended: She announced remission in January 2025 and completed the Three Peaks Challenge in June 2026 for The Royal Marsden Cancer Charity.

Story: Marc Márquez wins eighth MotoGP title in Portugal, surpassing Rossi's record
What happened: Marc Márquez needed surgery after a sprint crash at the French Grand Prix in Le Mans, missed a round and fell 102 points behind.
How it ended: He fought back from the Hungarian Grand Prix and clinched his record eighth MotoGP world title at the Portuguese Grand Prix.

Story: Near death experience sparked new career farming mushrooms
What happened: Nine years ago, Emma Court needed emergency brain surgery for an inflammatory mass that engulfed her pituitary gland and crushed an optic nerve.
How it ended: After surgery, immunotherapy and years of treatment, she built Rocky Creek Mushrooms, which won a silver medal at the 2026 Melbourne Royal food awards.

Story: WA housing department apologises to tenants for maintenance delays and moves them
What happened: Tanya Spider and Robin Dann waited more than two years for repairs to their Derby public housing home, with holes, rats and power cuts.
How it ended: After ABC questions, the WA housing department apologised, moved them to temporary accommodation and found them a new permanent property.

Story: Irish Kidney Association honours organ donor families
What happened: David Walsh from Aghabullogue, Co Cork, spent more than three years on dialysis.
How it ended: He received a deceased donor kidney transplant this year, on the 23rd anniversary of his baby daughter Michaela's death.

Story: Kicker told to amputate leg after cancer diagnosis beats the odds to resume pro sports career
What happened: Kicker Henry Nell was diagnosed with parosteal osteosarcoma behind his knee in 2025, and a local oncologist recommended amputating his leg.
How it ended: After limb-preserving surgery in July 2025, he returned to play for the Kansas Barrels and remains cancer-free, his surgeon said.

Story: What went right this week: the good news that matters
What happened: Jason Jones challenged Trinidad and Tobago's colonial-era law criminalising gay sex in 2017; the government partly reversed his High Court win.
How it ended: The Privy Council in London ruled in his favour, ending his near-decade-long legal campaign.

Story: Minister grants study visas to 48 students from Gaza after High Court challenge
What happened: Gaza students offered Irish university places faced visa refusals during the war; about 83% of 138 Palestinian long-stay applications were refused this year.
How it ended: After a High Court challenge, the Minister granted visas to 48 students, including five dance students whose University of Limerick fees were waived.

Story: Teen becomes viral cooking sensation after stepping up to feed his family amid mom's cancer battle
What happened: Jennifer Charney, a mother of eight in Augusta, Georgia, died in August after a 10-year battle with breast cancer.
How it ended: Her son Joey, 18, with no culinary training, took over the family cooking and now has more than 2 million followers.

Story: No qualifying stories
Toddler rescued after walking into remote area of Arizona desert
What happened: A 2-year-old girl walked about a mile and a half from home into remote Arizona desert, wearing only a diaper as temperatures dropped.
How it ended: Volunteer and neighbour Jay Stewart found her just after midnight Wednesday during the Pinal County Sheriff's Office search.

Story: 'Huna' wins National Book Award, but author denied visa to attend ceremony
What happened: Abdelrahman ElGendy spent six years as a political prisoner in Egypt from age 17 and smuggled his memoir out a few pages at a time.
How it ended: His memoir 'Huna' won the National Book Award for nonfiction; the US denied him a visa to attend the ceremony.

Story: No qualifying stories
'We don't count on anyone' – How Ukraine's internally displaced people struggle for housing
What happened: Iryna Cherkasova fled Luhansk in 2014 and Sievierodonetsk in 2022, then lived about two years with her family in a shared shelter room.
How it ended: Cherkasova found work and moved to a rented apartment; Veronika Chumak's Dnipro shelter, opened for evacuees, now houses 148 people.

Story: No qualifying stories
Qld man calls for action after almost 3hr ambulance wait 'bleeding out'
What happened: Veterinary nurse Carl Hartnett cut a major vein in a fall and waited almost three hours for an ambulance, losing about 1.3 litres of blood.
How it ended: Paramedics started IV fluids; after plastic and orthopaedic surgery in Brisbane he says paramedics saved his life.

Story: Doctors said Tisha would not survive the weekend, 30 years later she is thriving
What happened: Tisha Lourens was born premature with foetal alcohol syndrome and abandoned in hospital; staff said she would die that weekend.
How it ended: Adopted by Vivien Lourens, Tisha is now 30, works part-time at Merrypak and does awareness work.

Story: No qualifying stories
Funding deadline looms for outback rescue helicopter
What happened: As a toddler, Jack Martin fell into a campsite fire pit at Carnarvon Gorge, degloving his arms and burning them to the bone.
How it ended: LifeFlight flew him to Brisbane's children's burns unit; after six weeks of surgeries he survived and now has use of his left hand.

Story: 19 people rescued after gas carrier 'struck' in Black Sea
What happened: The LPG carrier Gas Husky was struck and overturned in Bulgaria's Black Sea economic zone, leaving its 19 crew in a life raft.
How it ended: A Bulgarian air force survey found the raft; all 19 crew were rescued and flown by helicopter to Chaika air base in Varna.

Story: No qualifying stories
Helen Haines 'full of gratitude' for medical care, in first statement since alleged attack
What happened: Independent MP Helen Haines, 65, lost both legs after being struck by a LandCruiser outside her Wangaratta office on October 19.
How it ended: She was discharged from Melbourne's Alfred hospital about four weeks later and has moved into rehabilitation.

Story: The split-second decision that saved Stuart Diver's life in Thredbo
What happened: Stuart Diver was trapped for 65 hours in the 1997 Thredbo landslide, which killed 18 people, including his wife Sally.
How it ended: He was pulled out alive and airlifted to Canberra Hospital; he was the only survivor.

Story: Surrogacy enables Queensland mum with kidney condition to have a family
What happened: Bec Vallee was diagnosed with nephrotic syndrome at 12, had two kidney transplants and was warned about the risks of pregnancy.
How it ended: Colleague Amanda Lewis carried her second daughter, Eva, born on August 3; her sister had been her first surrogate.

Story: 'Miracle on the Mississippi': All passengers rescued after tanker collides with cruise ship in New Orleans
What happened: The tanker Atlantic Asphalt hit the docked cruise ship American Heritage in New Orleans; the ship flipped and was partly submerged.
How it ended: The Port of New Orleans said all 197 passengers and crew were accounted for, with no critical injuries reported.

Story: 41-year-old firefighter's life saved by heart transplant
What happened: New Jersey firefighter Nico Ratto, 41, a father of two, spent 45 days in hospital before he could get a new heart.
How it ended: He received a heart transplant, which ABC News reports saved his life.

Story: Police find teenager alive six days after he disappeared in Gippsland bush
What happened: William, 17, went missing while camping near Walhalla East, fell down a riverbed embankment and spent six days lost in the bush.
How it ended: A police helicopter crew found him alive and winched him out; he was reunited with his mother and taken to hospital.

Story: After 40 years, Chilean mother reunites with two children stolen during dictatorship
What happened: During Pinochet's dictatorship, Teresita de Jesús Padilla's babies were taken from her at a hospital and trafficked to the United States for adoption.
How it ended: After about 41 years, Padilla met and embraced her sons Tim Rolnick and Travis Murdoch in Santiago.

Story: Baby buried alive for 24 hours released from the hospital; father charged
What happened: Michael Comer took his 11-month-old son Koah Sharpe; the baby was found after about 24 hours, shallowly buried in a dog crate in woods.
How it ended: Koah was released from hospital to family members and is expected to make a full recovery, authorities said; Comer is charged with attempted murder.

Story: Actor, 85, takes to the stage despite Alzheimer's diagnosis
What happened: Actor Peter Marinker, 85, was diagnosed with Alzheimer's after having difficulties during rehearsals for a previous production.
How it ended: He performed solo as Krapp in Beckett's Krapp's Last Tape for a four-day run at London's Cockpit Theatre in September.

Story: Australian veteran Ian Hart awarded medals 80 years after concluding service
What happened: Ian Hart served in the Pacific from 1944, but missing records led to his veterans' card being refused and he never received his medals.
How it ended: After his local RSL verified his service, the 100-year-old received five service medals, including the Pacific Star, and was honoured at state Parliament House.

Story: Officer shot 6 times celebrates wedding
What happened: Buffalo Police Officer Marc Hurst was shot six times while on duty.
How it ended: About five months later, he married his fiancée, Haley.

Story: Michael Betteridge and Hugh Page named as survivors of Indonesia helicopter crash
What happened: Pilots Michael Betteridge and Hugh Page were in a firefighting helicopter that nosedived into Borneo's Barito River; their navigator died.
How it ended: Both survived, were pulled from the water and treated at a military hospital.

Story: Queensland government aims to close gap in homelessness response
What happened: Ethan Shrubb slept rough for 18 months while battling addiction.
How it ended: He has lived in an inner-Brisbane apartment for two months, works in a warehouse and is studying IT.

Story: Australia-first co-housing project dubbed a 'perfect solution' for older women
What happened: After a divorce left her struggling financially, Ann Singh, 79, moved between rentals and house-sitting without a secure home.
How it ended: She moved into her own unit in a Darra, Brisbane co-housing project; five women each paid $120,000 for a 50-year lease.

Story: For queer people such as Stuart, community sport can be life-saving
What happened: Stuart Bonner, 31, was bullied at school in Glasgow after being outed and has a history of suicidal ideation and suicide attempts.
How it ended: He found belonging at LGBTQIA+ inclusive club Melbourne Rovers and became its president in 2025.

Story: Lebanese footballer refuses to give up after injuries from Israeli strike
What happened: Former Lebanon national footballer Celine Haidar, 21, was left in a coma and partially paralysed by an Israeli air strike on Beirut.
How it ended: She is rebuilding her life and is back on the pitch coaching young players.

Story: Connecting community through sport celebrated at Indigenous Sports Awards
What happened: As a child, Nat Heath was diagnosed with Guillain-Barré syndrome, which causes paralysis; a doctor said his endurance would never recover.
How it ended: He has competed in six Ironman events, won an age-division championship, and founded TriMob, now nominated for Team of the Year.

Story: Gaza: Displaced Palestinian builds wind turbine to generate electricity
What happened: Displaced to the al-Mawasi camp, with much of Gaza's power grid destroyed, Kamal Al-Dabary, 60, could not afford solar panels costing nearly $5,000.
How it ended: He built working wind turbines from scooter motors, water tanks and salvaged parts; they power phones, lights and fans for families without electricity.

Story: Newcastle woman who grew up in care now encouraging others to become foster carers
What happened: Rose Taylor entered foster care at 12, had five placements and two refuges by almost 16, and was homeless in Parramatta at 15.
How it ended: A teacher and later a colleague took her in; she finished school and now recruits foster carers at Life Without Barriers.

Story: 6-year-old boy found safe 2 days after going missing in rural Kentucky
What happened: Roman Heilman, 6, who has autism, went missing Sunday near his Louisa home; over 300 volunteers searched rugged woods for two days.
How it ended: He emerged Tuesday morning with his dog about 1.5 miles from home, scratched, and is recovering from dehydration in hospital.

Story: Palestinians return to ruined Hebron homes after Israel's 10-day siege
What happened: A 10-day Israeli operation in Hebron after two soldiers were shot dead on October 23 displaced about 3,300 people, including Fahd Ahmaro's family.
How it ended: After the forces withdrew, the displaced residents returned home; many houses are damaged and uninhabitable.

Story: Indian navy rescues 20 crew from Iranian fishing boat hijacked off Somalia
What happened: Suspected pirates hijacked the Iranian fishing boat Azini and its crew off Somalia's coast on October 29.
How it ended: Indian naval forces freed the boat and crew on November 2 after a 48-hour operation; India reported no casualties or injuries.

Story: Sisters go from lifesaving surgery to running a marathon
What happened: Kate Stevens had cancer and needed a bone marrow transplant, which her sister donated.
How it ended: Stevens survived, and about two decades later she ran a marathon alongside her sister.

Story: Actor Olivia Hargroder just wants a 'red hot go'
What happened: Olivia Hargroder, born with Down syndrome and a serious heart condition, had heart surgery at nine weeks with a 20 per cent survival chance.
How it ended: Now 27 and NIDA-trained, she plays the lead in the feature film Boss Cat, which premiered at the Sydney Film Festival in June.

Story: Five people rescued in Kiribati after drifting at sea for nearly three months
What happened: Nine people on a one-hour boat crossing in Micronesia on July 30 were caught in a storm and drifted about 5,400 km.
How it ended: Fanning Island villagers rescued five survivors, including two children, on November 1; local medics treated them. Four remain missing.

Story: What went right this week: the good news that matters
What happened: Tony Chapman was diagnosed with melanoma, a skin cancer, in 2019.
How it ended: He is cancer-free after taking part in a trial of the bespoke cancer vaccine intismeran; results are not yet peer-reviewed.

Story: 'Kickstart' gift helps Victorian man escape homelessness
What happened: Jake Dell'Aquila was homeless for over a year, sleeping in a tent on a Rosebud beach with his dog, unable to get housing help.
How it ended: Neighbour Dorothy Maafu bought him a caravan and six months of park bookings; he has since found work and a rental.

Story: No qualifying stories
Woman was 'one step from death' after leaving her violent partner
What happened: After years of abuse by a former partner, Jennifer was admitted to a mental health facility with PTSD, psychosis, depression and suicidal ideation.
How it ended: After treatment and support she rebuilt her life and says she now feels healthy and grounded; the court case against her ex continues.

Story: Gaza's women filmmakers turn pain into cinema as new academy launches
What happened: Three years of war destroyed Gaza's cultural venues; women filmmakers such as Mona Abu Qass worked through hunger, displacement, power and internet cuts.
How it ended: 25 women in a diploma programme produced five documentaries that opened the second Gaza International Women's Film Festival as the Gaza Cinema Academy launched.

Story: Fisherman found dehydrated adrift in Kiribati after 41 days lost at sea
What happened: Luka Rahan, 18, drifted for 41 days after his boat's motor failed on a fishing trip from Bougainville; his cousin reportedly died at sea.
How it ended: Kiribati fishermen found him between Tarawa and Maiana, about 2,000 km away; he is recovering in hospital before being sent home.

Story: How Venezuela's earthquake amputees adapt to life without limbs
What happened: Trapped under rubble in Venezuela's June 24 earthquakes, Ricardo Contreras, 24, lost his left leg; his parents died in the collapse.
How it ended: He is back at work in the family truck parts business and back at university on a full scholarship.

Story: 4 rescued on third day after Kenya building collapse as families lose hope
What happened: Tailor Victor Onyango and shop owner Zaynaba Mohammed were trapped when an 18-story building collapsed in Nairobi on October 23.
How it ended: Both were pulled out alive, treated in hospital and discharged; two more people were rescued alive on Sunday.

Story: Venezuela opposition leader María Corina Machado returns to country
What happened: Treated as a fugitive by Venezuela's government, María Corina Machado left secretly in December and was denied entry three times in one day in September.
How it ended: Her team confirmed on October 25 that she is back in Venezuela after nearly a year in exile.

Story: Usman Khawaja reveals illness he kept secret his entire Test cricket career
What happened: Diagnosed with rheumatoid arthritis at 22, Usman Khawaja at one point struggled to walk and kept the condition from teammates throughout his Test career.
How it ended: Treatment returned him to cricket within about six months; he played 88 Tests, scored 6,229 runs and retired after the January 2026 Ashes win.

Story: New documentary spotlights the 'silent killer' disproportionately affecting First Nations Australians
What happened: Kelli Owen, with genetic kidney disease Alport syndrome, spent about three years on dialysis from age 41, driving to Adelaide every second day.
How it ended: She received a donor kidney in 2016 and now works as a public health researcher at Adelaide University.

Story: No qualifying stories
'We're unbreakable': Ex-Israeli hostage's message to Bondi attack survivors
What happened: Hamas militants abducted IDF soldier Daniella Gilboa from the Nahal Oz post on 7 October 2023 and held her in Gaza.
How it ended: Freed in a January 2025 hostage-prisoner exchange, Gilboa, 22, made her international singing debut at the Sydney Opera House.

Story: U.S. citizen Stephen Hubbard released by Russia after 4 years in jail, and Trump says 'no swap'
What happened: Retired Michigan teacher Stephen Hubbard, 74, was captured in Ukraine in 2022, sentenced to nearly seven years, and held over four years.
How it ended: Russia freed him without a prisoner swap during Steve Witkoff's St. Petersburg visit; he was to be flown to Texas for treatment.

Story: Parwana Afghan Kitchen says Michelin recognition a great honour
What happened: Fleeing Soviet-occupied Kabul on foot, the Ayubi family spent about a year in a Pakistan refugee camp before reaching Australia in 1987.
How it ended: Their Adelaide restaurant Parwana, run since 2009, received a Bib Gourmand in the first Michelin Guide South Australia.

Story: Ukraine's military evacuates wounded soldier with aerial drone in apparent world-first
What happened: Soldier Konstantyn Vlasenko was trapped almost 500 days at a mined front-line position; wounded by a drone, he reportedly partially amputated both legs himself.
How it ended: Ukraine's 92nd Assault Brigade says a heavy-lift drone flew him nearly 40 miles to friendly territory in about 75 minutes.

Story: No qualifying stories
No qualifying stories
Siblings from Vanuatu with same rare birth defect can walk after donated Canberra care
What happened: Anis, 13, and Melanie, 3, from Tanna, Vanuatu, were born with severe clubfoot that went untreated until their feet turned backwards.
How it ended: After seven months of donated physiotherapy and surgery in Canberra, both children can walk; the family was preparing to fly home.

Story: Reema El Qassem is carving new pathways for disabled women in wheelchair basketball
What happened: Reema El Qassem, a single mother of four, acquired Functional Neurological Disorder in 2023 and spent 320 days in hospital.
How it ended: She plays for the Sydney Uni Lions as the league's first non-verbal player; the team reached the 2025 and 2026 playoffs.

Story: A 26-year-old felt her concerns were being dismissed. Then she was diagnosed with breast cancer.
What happened: Andrea de Armas was diagnosed with breast cancer at 26, the day before her physician assistant program began.
How it ended: After a lumpectomy and chemotherapy scheduled around classes, she is cancer-free at 30 and graduated from her PA program in 2025.

Story: After four attempts, woman's dying wish to see brother finally granted
What happened: Bed-bound with avascular necrosis, Anna Rochford spent over a year trying to bring her brother Clinton Barrett from India; Home Affairs kept refusing his visa.
How it ended: The fourth application was approved after media coverage and the local MP's intervention, and Barrett arrived to stay by her side.

Story: Pope Leo XIV celebrates Mass as recovery from cancer surgery progresses
What happened: Pope Leo XIV was hospitalised at Rome's Gemelli Hospital for lung cancer surgery.
How it ended: His doctors say his post-operative recovery lets him carry out normal daily activities completely on his own; he has celebrated Mass.

Story: Dallas woman rebuilds her life with help from Austin Street Center's Sisterhood Program
What happened: After her husband died about 10 years ago, Maggie Williams developed a drug addiction, lost her job and home, and lived in her car.
How it ended: She entered Austin Street Center's Sisterhood Program this summer and is now moving into her own apartment.

Story: Cosumnes River College fire program helps woman find hope amid tragedy
What happened: Kayla Kerney's husband Harlin died a few years ago, leaving her to raise two young children.
How it ended: She trained in Cosumnes River College's fire technology program and received a full-time firefighter offer from the Cosumnes Fire Department.

Story: Calls for better post-cancer care to give isolated survivors support
What happened: Carly Gogel of Naracoorte was diagnosed with stage two Hodgkin's lymphoma before turning 24 and spent about a year in treatment.
How it ended: She has been cancer-free for five years, received counselling through Canteen and has returned to work.

Story: Indigenous preschools teach language and culture to young and old
What happened: Gumbaynggirr elder Julie Craig, 65, never learned her language; her grandparents died young, her parents didn't speak it, and schools banned it until 1972.
How it ended: She now learns Gumbaynggirr alongside her great-granddaughter Enalanii at Kulai Preschool, which added formal language programs in 2022.

Story: Arnhem Land nurse Yiwarr McGrath enters parliament as Labor's new Member for Mulka
What happened: Yiwarr McGrath lost his father at five and his mother at ten, and grew up in poverty across remote Arnhem Land outstations.
How it ended: He became a registered nurse, won the Mulka by-election for Labor and was sworn into the NT Parliament.

Story: Australian engineer Robert Pether allowed to leave Iraq five years after arrest
What happened: Engineer Robert Pether was arrested in Iraq in 2021 on fraud charges he denies, jailed over four years, then barred from leaving.
How it ended: Foreign Minister Penny Wong confirmed he has left Baghdad; he is travelling to reunite with his family in Ireland.

Story: Billy Crystal on finding humor in the darkest of times
What happened: The January 2025 Pacific Palisades wildfire destroyed Billy Crystal's family home; in December 2025 his friends Rob and Michelle Reiner were killed.
How it ended: He turned the loss into a one-man Broadway show, "860", now in previews and opening October 21 at the Imperial Theatre.

The girls in the Gaza school photograph

How it ended: Yasmin survived and now studies psychology; Ghaida Zaqout began dentistry in Egypt; Yasmin and Lina Yunis Abd al-Qader reunited with their teacher.
